“Verify” is a little loose yeah. In practice, it has been pretty useful for Claude to do something like:

1. Build a model of the program, targeting a tricky state machine or race-prone part of the code
2. Find counter-examples in the model: these are suspected bugs 
3. Reproduce the bugs
4. Fix the bugs

Cliff compactin is very easy to install and use with Codex, Claude Code and is integrated in bitsandbytes code our harness for autnomous research.

Install: pip install cliffcompaction
Use: cliff enable

It works by managing a separate compaction state between you and any OpenAI/Anthropic API

reviewedPosts.author: Tim_Dettmers

CliffCompaction might be unintuitive at first. It deliberately throws away context after two compactions, but it has a purpose.

The main cause of context drift is when agents read a summary that misses critical information but continue working, thinking they have everything.
